ImageDescription.value: A meticulous architectural model of the Kalon Minaret (Minorai Kalon) and its adjacent madrasa in Bukhara. This detailed replica offers a unique top-down and frontal perspective, highlighting the distinctive brickwork patterns of the minaret and the elegant ceramic mosaic façade of the madrasa portal. It masterfully showcases the intricacy and geometry characteristic of medieval Central Asian folk art and Islamic architecture, preserving the visual impact of the original heritage site in a tangible form.

ImageDescription.value:
500px provided description: Bukhara is an ancient city in the central Asian country of Uzbekistan. It was a prominent stop on the Silk Road trade route between the East and the West, and a major medieval center for Islamic theology and culture. It still contains hundreds of well-preserved mosques, madrassas, bazaars and caravanserais, dating largely from the 9th to the 17th centuries.

Early morning in Bukhara?The golden light lights up the Poi-Kalan Ensemble, which is the main ensemble in Bukhara center, situated on the way to trade crossing of "four bazars". Poi-Kalan means ?the pedestal of the Great? (it means ?the pedestal of Kalyan minaret?) and the ensemble consists of 4 monuments: Kalyan mosque and Mini-Arab Madrasah ? faced to each other with main fronts; between them is Kalyan minaret.
